column2: On the authority of al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The son of Ādam fills no vessel worse than his stomach. It is enough for the son of Ādam to have a few morsels to keep his back upright.
But if he must, then a third for food, a third for drink and a third for breath.” Reported by Imam Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah; al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan hadith.
“It is enough for the son of Ādam”: it suffices him to keep himself alive.
Luqaymāt (“a few morsels”): the diminutive of luqmah (a mouthful).
“To keep his back (ṣulbahu) upright”: his spine, so that he has strength for worship and work.
“But if he must”: go beyond that,
“then a third for food”: what he eats,
“and a third for drink”: what he drinks,
“and a third for breath”: so that he can breathe lightly and easily.
Eating little and not eating much.
One should make one's eating and drinking in the proportion of a third for food, a third for drink and a third for breath.
Whoever exceeds this measure has gone against what the Prophet ﷺ guided to.
This hadith guides to complete prevention for the preservation of a person's health.
Whoever does not act on what is in this hadith has exposed himself to deadly diseases, sooner or later.

The noble Prophet ﷺ guides us to one of the principles of medicine, namely prevention, by which a person protects his health: eating little; rather, one eats as much as keeps him alive and strengthens him for his necessary tasks.

The worst vessel to be filled is the stomach, because of the countless deadly diseases that result from satiety, sooner or later, internal or external. Then the Messenger ﷺ said: if a person must eat his fill,

let him make his food a third, another third for drink, and a third for breath, so that he does not suffer constriction, harm, or laziness in fulfilling what Allah has made obligatory on him in his religious or worldly affairs: “And eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not love the excessive” [al-Aʿrāf 7:31].

So a person should adopt the manners of the Sharīʿah, obey the command of the Messenger ﷺ and preserve his health; for as it is said: prevention is better than cure; and as it is said: the stomach is the house of disease.
Whenever you give your stomach what it asks for, / and your private parts too, the two together attain the utmost of blame.
